newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius rupee firms on dlr, forex demand lower.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius rupee firms on dlr, forex demand lower.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee firmed against the dollar and was stable versus the pound on Friday, reflecting a combined effect of international trends and a drop in foreign exchange demand, commercial banks forex dealers said.
The rupee traded at a mean rate of 20.6325 for one dollar on Friday from 20.6445 on Thursday. The rupee was fixed unchanged against the pound on Friday at a mean rate of 32.329.
Forex dealers said the rupee was fixed firmer against the dollar because of the U.S. currency's softness in overnight international markets and lower foreign exchange demand from banks' customers.
This took some pressure of the local currency.

"We recently had to face increased demand from customers (importers) entering in forward contracts. This quickly made banks reserves short and was putting weakening pressure on the rupee," one commercial dealer said.
"The pressure was relieved by the two central bank market interventions this week," the dealer added.
The central bank sold dollars in the interbank forex market on Monday and Wednesday last.
"With the rupee being more or less stable against the dollar now, demand has fallen and banks no longer appear to be short," the dealer added.
More foreign exchange inflow was seen entering the interbank forex market on Friday morning with a Mauritius Sugar Syndicate tender sale of pounds obtained from the country's sugar export proceeds.
